pattern.description: X is closer to Y than to other alternatives (X is more similar to Y than to other approaches, indicating a degree of methodological proximity).
pattern.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly positioned as more similar or proximal to another than to alternatives; not for general comparison, ranking, or shared-feature listing.

mutations.evidence: approach that is closer to the established methods of Chapman–Enskog gas theory
mutations.rationale: HE7 expresses a comparative proximity ('closer to') between an approach and established methods. This is not 'extends' (no generalization), not 'improves' (no limitation fix), not 'compares' (no side-by-side evaluation of two alternatives), and not 'analogous_to' (which asserts similarity without the comparative degree). This is a distinct relation: X is more similar to Y than to other options. The existing 'compares' pattern requires putting two things side by side, but here the focus is on relative similarity, not evaluation.

pattern.description: X is validated/verified by comparison with Y (X's predictions or results are checked against Y, which could be experimental data or another theory).
pattern.semantic_boundary: Use when one method’s output is explicitly checked against another method’s output or data; not for mere comparison, co-use, or one method generating the other.

pattern.description: X contrasts with Y in terms of scope, assumptions, or applicability (X and Y have different strengths/weaknesses, often complementary).
pattern.semantic_boundary: Use when two methods are explicitly compared as alternatives with trade-offs; NOT for simple co-occurrence, sequential use, or one method merely improving another.
